title: Economic Stewardship in the Next American Founding
gist: David Ciepley (excerpt before paywall) argues the corporation is fundamentally a governance device for dedicating property to a purpose under stewards, and that the business corporation has drifted from this in recent decades. He sketches three corporate eras and three waves of business corporations, ending in today's mobile, short-term 'neoliberal' corporation, and links economic reform to every American re-founding.

insights.claim: Ciepley identifies three corporate eras: medieval ecclesiastical corporations (monasteries, cathedral chapters, early universities), late-medieval to early-modern civil corporations (towns, guilds), and the business corporation era from early modernity to today.

insights.so_what: Suggests lead institutions rotate historically, so the business corporation's primacy is not permanent.
